question: What is the primary goal of a quality assurance committee in healthcare?

options.A: To increase hospital revenue and patient turnover rates
options.B: To continuously monitor, evaluate, and improve the delivery of patient care
options.C: To discipline healthcare workers who violate hospital policies
options.D: To manage the financial budgets of the clinical departments

explanation: The primary goal of a QA committee is to systematically monitor, evaluate, and improve patient care delivery against established guidelines. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which regulatory body sets standards that Nigerian nurses and quality committees must align with?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) is a key regulatory body setting professional standards for nursing practice in the country. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary structure essential for a quality assurance committee?

options.A: It ensures that multiple professional perspectives are considered when evaluating clinical processes.
options.B: It allows physicians to make all clinical decisions without input from others.
options.C: It reduces the total number of hospital staff required to work night shifts.
options.D: It guarantees that hospital funding will be spent exclusively on administrative tasks.

explanation: A multidisciplinary team brings together varied perspectives from physicians, nurses, and administrators to comprehensively evaluate hospital operations. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: What makes nurses particularly valuable members of a quality assurance committee?

options.A: They control the financial budget of the hospital.
options.B: They write all hospital medical prescriptions.
options.C: They constitute the largest workforce and have frontline experience in patient care.
options.D: They are exclusively responsible for hospital legal matters.

explanation: Nurses make up the largest workforce and provide frontline care, giving them crucial insights into daily clinical workflows and patient safety hazards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is a core responsibility of a quality assurance committee?

options.B: Establishing clinical audit schedules and reviewing institutional policies
options.C: Directly hiring and firing all hospital nursing staff
options.D: Managing the personal financial accounts of physicians

explanation: QA committees are responsible for establishing clinical audits and reviewing policies against current healthcare standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h3)

question: In resource-constrained settings, what type of interventions should a quality assurance committee prioritize?

options.A: Interventions that yield the highest impact on patient safety like infection control
options.B: Purchasing luxury furnishings for executive waiting rooms
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing shifts per week

explanation: The committee prioritizes high-impact safety interventions such as infection control and safe medication administration to maximize patient outcomes. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is a clinical audit?

options.A: A financial check of hospital billing systems
options.B: A systematic review of patient health records against predetermined standards
options.C: An evaluation of nurse working hours and salary structures
options.D: A test of hospital electrical and plumbing infrastructure

explanation: A clinical audit systematically reviews patient health records against established standards to measure the quality of care delivered. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following patient outcomes is directly influenced by the quality of nursing care provided?

options.A: Incidence of pressure ulcers and patient falls
options.B: Hospital electricity and water supply consistency

explanation: Nursing care directly impacts metrics such as pressure ulcer prevalence, patient falls, and hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a non-punitive incident reporting system?

options.A: To punish staff members who make minor paperwork mistakes
options.B: To encourage workers to report errors and safety hazards without fear of victimization
options.C: To hide hospital mistakes from regulatory authorities
options.D: To increase the workload of nursing supervisors

explanation: A non-punitive system encourages staff to report errors openly so the root causes can be analyzed and fixed without fear of punishment. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: What analytical tool does the committee use to determine why a reported adverse incident occurred?
explanation: Root cause analysis (RCA) is used to investigate systemic issues and determine the underlying reasons behind an adverse event. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of collecting and analyzing performance metrics in a QA committee?

options.A: To evaluate trends, benchmark performance, and check if quality improvements are working
options.B: To determine individual nurse salary increments and bonuses
options.C: To comply with tax collection laws for healthcare businesses
options.D: To increase the volume of paper documents stored in the hospital

explanation: Performance metrics are analyzed to identify trends, compare against standards, and evaluate the effectiveness of quality improvements. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is a major data-related transition happening in many Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: Moving from digital systems entirely back to oral storytelling
options.B: Transitioning from manual paper-based records to digital health information systems
options.C: Eliminating all patient recordkeeping to save storage space
options.D: Outsourcing data analysis to foreign travel agencies

explanation: Many facilities are working on transitioning from manual paper records to digital health information systems to improve data accuracy. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the difference between corrective actions and preventive actions in a CAPA framework?

options.A: Corrective actions fix existing errors, while preventive actions proactively stop potential errors before they occur.
options.B: Corrective actions are for doctors, while preventive actions are exclusively for hospital administrators.
options.C: Corrective actions cost money, whereas preventive actions are entirely free of charge.
options.D: Corrective actions are optional, while preventive actions are illegal.

explanation: Corrective actions address existing problems, while preventive actions proactively anticipate and stop potential errors from happening. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of a preventive action?

options.A: Reprimanding a nurse after a medication error occurs
options.B: Redesigning a medication chart layout to prevent look-alike, sound-alike drug mix-ups
options.C: Closing an entire hospital ward following an outbreak
options.D: Filing an incident report after a patient fall has already happened

explanation: Redesigning a chart layout to stop drug mix-ups before they happen is a proactive, preventive measure. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge faced by QA committees in Nigerian hospitals?

options.B: Funding constraints, infrastructural deficits, and staff shortages
options.C: Zero interest in patient care from any clinical staff
options.D: Absence of any medical errors in the healthcare system

explanation: Nigerian hospitals often face challenges such as funding constraints, infrastructural deficits, and staff shortages which impact QA operations. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is considered a best practice for overcoming operational challenges in hospital QA committees?

options.A: Fostering strong leadership commitment and integrating QA training into education
options.B: Punishing staff members heavily whenever an audit reveals a minor flaw
options.C: Halting all incident reporting until infrastructure is completely modernized
options.D: Excluding nurses from committee meetings to save time

explanation: Strong leadership and integrating QA training into staff education are key best practices for sustaining effective quality committees. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)
